extraction_text: Sage Shaunaka asks the Suta (Sauti) to name the snakes that fell into the sacrificial fire during the snake sacrifice.

attributes.relationships: Shaunaka is a sage inquiring; Sauti is the narrator (son of Lomaharshana, the 'Suta' or bard)

extraction_text: Sauti explains that countless snakes perished, too many to name all, but he will recount the names of the main ones remembered and spoken of by people.
Sauti lists the main snakes born in the Vasuki family that fell into the fire: green, red, and white ones, fierce in form, with long bodies full of venom.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Snakes with venomous and fearsome attributes

extraction_text: Specific names of Vasuki's offspring are given: Frogs, Mind, Plump, Capable, Interceptor, Plough-holder, Slippery, Destroyer, Wheel, Corner-fierce, Pursuer, Golden Horse, Arrow, Dry Wood, and Death's Tooth.
Sauti lists snakes born in the Takshaka family that fell into the fire.

Specific names of Takshaka's offspring are given: Tail-egg, Round, Pindapeta, Ropenaka, High-crown, Delicious-taste, For-city, Powerful-anger, Sprouting, Holder-of-vows, Stick-maker, Silent, Beautiful-child, Shaker, Great-mace, Rabbit-hair, Beautiful-thought, and Swift-runner.
Sauti lists snakes born in the Airavata family that fell into the fire: Distant, Whirling, Pale-white, Pale-yellow, Slender, Sky-goer, Eight-legged-monster, Joyful, Ecstatic, and Healthy-body.

attributes.relationships: All are offspring of Airavata family

extraction_text: Sauti lists snakes born in the Kauravya family: Beloved-leaver, Earring, Bald, Braid-on-shoulder, Little-child, Servant, Horned-fierce, Bad-seed, Pata, and Patala (twins).

attributes.relationships: All are offspring of Kauravya family

extraction_text: Sauti lists snakes born in the Dhritarashtra family: swift as wind, full of venom, including Sharp-ear, Crimson-yellow, Axe and Blue-face (pair), Plump-body, Round-mouth, Laughing, Great-bird, Ochre, Amahata, Kumarataka, Breath, Mortal, Fig-tree, Fearful, Bald Veda-branch, Reddish-brown, Water-piercer, Bull, Swift, Beggar and Great-jaw (pair), Red-body, All-spotted, Success, Vast, and Rakshasa (pair), Little-pig, Little-elephant, Beautiful-friend, Strange-talk, Smasher, Tender, Jewel-shoulder, and Dawn.

attributes.relationships: All are offspring of Dhritarashtra family

extraction_text: Sauti concludes that the named snakes are the most famous and main ones, but all snakes, including their countless descendants, fell into the fire, too numerous to list fully.

Sauti mentions that many seven-headed, two-headed, and five-headed snakes, terrifying like the fire at the end of an age, fell into the fire, along with huge snakes as tall as mountains and up to two yojanas in length.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Snakes with multiple heads, immense size, and venom compared to apocalyptic fire

extraction_text: King Janamejaya (son of Parikshit) attempted to perform a snake sacrifice to kill Takshaka, but Takshaka was suspended in mid-air and would not fall into the fire.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Takshaka suspended in mid-air by Indra

extraction_text: Astika shouted 'Stay! Stay! Stay!' three times at Takshaka, causing him to become fixed in mid-air.
King Janamejaya granted Astika's wish and stopped the snake sacrifice.
The sacrifice was halted, the snakes were saved, and there was great rejoicing.
King Janamejaya rewarded the priests and supervisors with hundreds of thousands of gold coins.
The bard Lomaharshana (also called 'Red-eyed') had predicted the sacrifice would be obstructed by a Brahmin, and was richly rewarded by the king.
King Janamejaya invited Astika to be a supervisor at his future Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice).

extraction_text: Astika returned joyfully to his mother and uncle, reported everything, and all the snakes rejoiced, their worries dispelled.
